# Texas Permit Guide (Austin-Area Residential Permit Cheat Sheet)

> Free summary of whether common home projects need a building permit in Austin, Round Rock, Pflugerville and Cedar Park, Texas, with base permit fees, wildfire (WUI) code rules, and a link to the city source for every answer. Sources last checked Oct 15, 2026. Informational only, not legal advice; confirm with the city before starting work.

Projects covered for each city: water heater, HVAC replacement, roof replacement, fence, deck / patio cover, shed / accessory building, solar PV, in-ground pool, electrical panel upgrade, irrigation system. Where no clear city answer was found, the sheet says "Check with city" instead of guessing. Fees are base permit fees only; plan review, technology or other fees may apply, and most cities update fees each October. Areas outside city limits (ETJ / unincorporated Travis or Williamson County) follow different rules.

Key facts:
- Austin: over half the city is in a Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) zone (A, B or C). WUI rules apply to permit applications on or after July 10, 2025; existing homes are not required to retrofit. WUI projects need residential plan review, product specs on plans, and two WUI inspections.
- Round Rock, Pflugerville and Cedar Park: no city WUI code found.
